classification.difficultyReason: Calculate the difference in post heights before using Pythagoras' theorem to find the string length.

content.prompt:
Two posts are 7.2 m tall and 9.6 m tall and 11 m apart on level ground.
Calculate the length of string required to stretch from the top of one post to the top of the other.
Round your answer to 1 d.p.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6 post diagram beneath the prompt
spec.description: Two unshaded upright posts with the shorter post on the left, a common horizontal ground line, right-angle markers at both bases and a straight string between the post tops.
spec.mathematics: The post heights are 7.2 m and 9.6 m, with horizontal separation 11 m. The string is the hypotenuse of a triangle with vertical leg equal to the height difference.
spec.answerVisibility: The three given measurements are visible. The height difference and string length are not supplied.
spec.intentionalSourceDeparture: Replaced decorative grey post shading and magenta string, ground line and right-angle markers with unshaded posts and black strokes. Measurements, geometry and original source evidence are preserved.

answer.worked:
The vertical difference is $9.6-7.2=2.4\text{ m}$.
Let $s$ be the string length.
$$\begin{align*}s &= \sqrt{11^2+2.4^2}\\s &= \sqrt{126.76}\\s &\approx 11.3\text{ m}\quad\text{(1 d.p.)}\end{align*}$$
